findings.title: Unsanitized `type` param flows into a shell command via the tempfile path (command injection)
findings.body: `type` comes directly from `params` and is embedded into the download tempfile name ("discourse-upload-#{type}") at line 55. This PR then passes `tempfile.path` to `OptimizedImage.downsize` (line 67), and `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes the instructions with backticks (`` `#{instructions.join(" ")}` `` in optimized_image.rb) with no shell escaping. A caller who can use the API URL-upload branch (`is_api?` + `url` present, no file) can put shell metacharacters such as `$(...)` or backticks into `type`; hosting an image larger than `max_image_size_kb` at that URL makes the new downsize branch execute, running the injected command as the app server user. Previously this tempfile path never reached a shell, so this exposure is introduced by this PR. Validate `type` against a whitelist before using it in a filename, and/or stop interpolating paths into a shell string (use an argv-array form of exec instead of backticks).

findings.title: self.downsize is defined twice; the 4-argument version is dead and old callers silently misbehave
findings.body: The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: lines 145-147 (`from, to, max_width, max_height, opts`) and lines 149-151 (`from, to, dimensions, opts`). Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the first method is dead code. Worse, any existing or plugin caller still using the old 4-argument form `downsize(from, to, width, height)` gets no arity error: the width is used verbatim as the ImageMagick geometry string (e.g. `-resize 1920\>` with no height) and the height (an Integer) is used as `opts`, so `!!opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` raises TypeError (Integer#[] with a Symbol), which is not rescued because the rescue lives in `convert_with`. Remove the leftover 4-argument definition (or make it delegate to the new one correctly).

findings.title: Large animated GIFs are silently flattened to their first frame
findings.body: The downsize call passes `tempfile.path` as `from`, and `OptimizedImage.optimize` only selects the animated (gifsicle) code path when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Upload tempfiles created by Rack (and the API download tempfile) do not carry the original file extension, so for normal composer uploads this check is always false and a large animated GIF is processed by `convert from[0] ...`, whose `[0]` selects only the first frame and writes a static image back over the user's original file — the animation is silently destroyed even when `allow_animation` is enabled. Additionally, even when the animated branch is reached, it is handed the geometry string "80%", but gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects an explicit WxH geometry and does not accept percentages, so it would fail on every one of the 5 attempts (the loop also ignores `downsize`'s false return and just retries the identical command). Base the animation check on the original filename or content type rather than the tempfile path, and use gifsicle-compatible geometry.

findings.title: Client upload size check hardcodes 10MB for all types, ignoring the per-type site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` now caps every upload at `10 * 1024` KB instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. The server-side downsize added in this PR only applies to images; attachments are still validated against `max_attachment_size_kb`, so sites with a lower attachment limit now accept files client-side that the server then rejects (bad UX, wasted upload), and sites with a higher attachment limit (or `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB) now have legitimate uploads blocked client-side — a regression. The 413 error handler at line 246 likewise always reports a 10MB limit in the `file_too_large` message regardless of the actual configured limit. Keep the per-type setting for attachments and only raise the effective cap for images that the server can downsize.

findings.title: API URL-download cap hardcoded to 10MB and nil tempfile still dereferenced
findings.body: For API uploads by URL the download limit was changed from the configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a fixed `10.megabytes`. This branch also serves non-image uploads, so attachments larger than 10MB can no longer be pulled via the API even when `max_attachment_size_kb` permits them. When the cap is exceeded the `rescue nil` leaves `tempfile` as nil, and line 72 then calls `tempfile.size`, raising NoMethodError instead of returning a clean error to the API client. Use the per-type size setting and handle the nil tempfile case explicitly.

findings.title: No tests for the new auto-downsize behavior
findings.body: The new downsize loop in `create_upload` (lines 64-70) — a retry loop that shells out to ImageMagick/gifsicle and mutates the uploaded file before `Upload.create_for` — ships without any spec coverage. There are no tests verifying that an over-limit image is downsized and accepted, that an image still over the limit after 5 attempts returns a clean validation error, or that animated GIFs keep their animation (they currently do not). Add controller/model specs covering these cases.
